newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC - no comment on Dillon Read report.
newsitem.headline: SBC - no comment on Dillon Read report.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp declined to comment on a newspaper report that SBC Warburg would buy Dillon Read & Co for about $600 million.
"We have absolutely no comment," a bank spokemsan said by telephone from Basle.
The Wall Street Journal reported SBC Warburg could announce a deal to acquire the U.S. investment bank as early as today.

SBC chief executive Marcel Ospel said last month that it company had no plans for a major investment banking acquisition in North America, but was on the lookout for possible deals to expand private banking.
Asked in the April edition of Euromoney magazine about rumours SBC was about to do something big in North America, Ospel said he was unaware of such talk.

"I can confirm there are no such plans. The market for U.S. investment banks is vastly overpriced. The ongoing dilution of the regulatory environment will change the landscape for investment and private banking in North America," he said.

"We want to know more about what will happen before we consider anything. However, if there was an opportunity here and there -- in particular to buy a franchise or expertise by acquiring a small boutique -- we'd consider it."
Banking analysts have stated in the past that a North American acquisition would make sense for SBC to round out its global operations.
Ospel had dismissed the idea of buying a second-tier U.S. investment bank.

"Some players in the second and third brackets have been on the market for a while. If we'd intended to buy one, we'd have moved a few years ago," he said, adding the approach of hiring away top people did not seem likely to be successful.
